entries.question: How should a coding interview response be scored? What differentiates a 3/10 from a 7/10 from a 10/10?
entries.expectedApproach: Score on multiple dimensions: correctness, efficiency, code quality, communication, edge cases.
keyPoints: Score 1-3 (Poor): Cannot identify the problem type. No working solution. Poor communication.
Score 4-5 (Below Average): Identifies approach but cannot implement fully. Brute force solution only. Misses edge cases.
Score 6-7 (Good): Working solution with reasonable efficiency. Handles most edge cases. Clean code. Good communication of thought process.
Score 8-9 (Excellent): Optimal or near-optimal solution. Handles all edge cases. Clean, production-quality code. Discusses trade-offs proactively.
Score 10 (Outstanding): Optimal solution with excellent code quality. Considers multiple approaches and justifies choice. Proactively discusses testing, scalability, and real-world applications.

entries.question: How should a system design interview response be evaluated? What are the key dimensions?
entries.expectedApproach: Evaluate on: requirements gathering, high-level design, component design, scalability, trade-offs discussion, and deep-dive knowledge.
keyPoints: Score 1-3 (Poor): Jumps into solution without clarifying requirements. Monolithic design with no scalability consideration. No discussion of trade-offs.
Score 4-5 (Below Average): Basic architecture but missing key components. Limited scalability discussion. Doesn't consider failure modes.
Score 6-7 (Good): Clear requirements gathering. Well-structured architecture. Discusses caching, load balancing, databases. Considers failure scenarios.

Score 8-9 (Excellent): Comprehensive design covering all aspects. Deep knowledge of distributed systems. Quantifies with back-of-envelope calculations. Proactively discusses monitoring and deployment.
Score 10 (Outstanding): All of the above plus novel insights, experience-backed recommendations, and clear articulation of why alternatives were not chosen.

entries.question: How should behavioral interview responses be evaluated? What makes a strong behavioral answer?
entries.expectedApproach: Use STAR method compliance, specificity, impact quantification, self-awareness, and growth demonstration.
keyPoints: Score 1-3 (Poor): Vague, hypothetical answers ('I would do X'). Cannot provide specific examples. Blames others for failures. No self-awareness.
Score 4-5 (Below Average): Real examples but lacking detail. No quantified impact. STAR method partially followed. Limited self-reflection.
Score 6-7 (Good): Clear STAR structure. Specific examples with measurable outcomes. Shows self-awareness and lessons learned. Demonstrates ownership.
Score 8-9 (Excellent): Strong stories with impressive impact. Multiple perspectives considered. Clear growth trajectory. Authentic and reflective.
Score 10 (Outstanding): Compelling narratives with exceptional impact. Shows leadership, mentoring, and org-wide influence. Deeply self-aware with a track record of continuous improvement.
